preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines() for x in line.split() if x.isdigit())
preconditions.description: All integers in input (N, M, P, and edge endpoints A, B) are within the bounds 1 ≤ N, M, P ≤ 10^5 and 1 ≤ A, B ≤ N.
The input has exactly M + 1 lines: the first line contains N, M, P, and the next M lines contain edges.
Each of the M edge lines contains exactly two integers (A and B).
The number of edges M does not exceed the maximum allowed (10^5 or the complete graph edges, whichever is larger).

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer representing the count of critical links.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout) == sum(1 for edge in edges if (is_bridge(edge, graph) and satisfies_size_condition(edge, graph, P)))
postconditions.description: The output equals the number of edges that are bridges (critical links) in the graph and satisfy the size condition: when removed, the graph splits into exactly one more connected component, and the difference in node counts between the two resulting components is less than P. Here, `edges` is the list of all edges in the graph, `graph` is the adjacency representation of the graph, `is_bridge(edge, graph)` checks if removing `edge` increases the number of connected components by exactly 1, and `satisfies_size_condition(edge, graph, P)` checks if the node count difference between the two resulting components is less than P.
